instructions.question: Is this Facebook comment on a Kosovo public-health COVID-19 post mainly positive, mainly negative (an attack, accusation, mockery or alarm), or neutral?
instructions.rule: Negative only when the main point is hostile or distressed: it claims the numbers are faked or copy-pasted or that the institute lies, mocks or scolds the institute or Albanians as a group, insults or swears, or voices alarm or despair that things are out of control. Questions, pointing out mismatched numbers, demands or suggestions for measures (even shouted), opinions about causes, short political remarks, town-ranking or betting banter, bare names, casual greetings to tagged friends, and cryptic or off-topic texts are neutral. Praise, thanks (even with a question), blessings, prayers and relief or good news about recoveries or falling numbers are positive.

neutral.what: Questions, number guesses, mismatched figures, demands or suggestions for measures, opinions, brief political remarks, banter, jokes, bare names, casual greetings, cryptic or off-topic texts.
examples: Mbyllni kufijte sot! (Close the borders today!)
Prap Prishtina spe lshon kreun e tabeles (Again Prishtina won't give up the top of the table)
Shes kepurdha (I sell mushrooms)
neutral.cues: pse/qysh/sa ? (why/how/how many ?); mbyllni/hapni (close/open); duhet (should); lige/tabele/bast (league/table/bet); tagged names; haha
neutral.not_for: Claims of deliberate faking or copy-paste, mockery or scolding of the institute or of Albanians, insults, and 'lost control' alarm are negative.

positive.what: Approval, thanks, blessings, prayers, and relief or good news about recoveries and falling numbers.
examples: Ju lumte per punen suksese! (Well done for the work, success!)
T'hajrit kofshin (May they be for good)
So keq sa per fillim (Not bad for a start)
Kur don zoti per bajram dalum 0-0 (God willing, by Bayram we come out 0-0)
positive.cues: bravo; ju lumte (well done); faleminderit (thank you); perhajr/t'hajrit (for good); me shnet (in health); amin (amen); zoti na ruajt (God protect us); inshallah (God willing); urime (congratulations); super lajm (great news); so keq/sosht keq (not bad); lutem (I pray)
positive.not_for: A bare name that is also a word ('Shpresë Koliqi') and casual greetings to friends ('aje mirë', 'mbajuni') are neutral; sarcastic blessings ('Kerrrk Na kofshi per hajr') are negative.

negative.what: Accusations of faked or copy-pasted numbers or lying, sarcastic mockery of the institute, scolding Albanians as a group, insults and swearing, alarm or despair.
examples: Dje 226 sod 224 mos jeni tja bo copy paste. (Yesterday 226, today 224, aren't you copy-pasting?)
Bajat jenii boo mooo pffff (You've become stale, pfff)
E hupi kontrollen e hupi Ferizaji (Ferizaj lost control)
Gjithqfare budall ka Kosova. (Kosovo has all kinds of fools.)
negative.cues: copy paste; rren/rrena (lies); a ju besohet (do you believe it yourselves); bajat (stale); jeni lodh (you're tired); si bastore/loto/KEK (like bettors/lottery/the power company); turp të kini (shame on you); budall (fool); nanen, mut (swearing); hupi kontrollen (lost control); kah po shkojmë (where are we heading)
negative.not_for: Plain questions about numbers, shouted demands for measures and banter about towns are neutral.
